title: Opus Mechanical Self-Drag Antipattern
desc: T1 reflex. When an expensive model (Opus) executes MECHANICAL work directly, it walks into the stacked guard maze and burns 10x time. Delegate mechanical to Haiku from the start. 2026-06-09 incident: Opus dragged a 1-function harness patch 10+ min; Haiku did it in 65s.
steps: TRIGGER: an expensive model (Opus) is about to execute MECHANICAL work directly -- a file edit, git, build, gh release, or harness patch.

REFLEX: STOP and delegate to Haiku or codex IMMEDIATELY. Opus executing mechanical work directly walks into the stacked guard maze (pace, stall, tier-gate) and burns roughly 10x the time fighting guards instead of doing the task.

INCIDENT 2026-06-09: Opus dragged a one-function stall-guard patch for 10-plus minutes through gemini-pace 954/500, then claude-pace 172 percent, then stall-guard, then tier-gate; the moment tier-gate cleared, a Haiku subagent applied the exact same edit in 65 seconds. Subagents are pace/wk-only exempt, so they sail through.

ROOT CAUSE: Opus value is judgment, decomposition, briefing, synthesis, and final review -- NOT mechanical execution. Pushing mechanical work through guards is the wrong-layer trap. Conduct, do not execute.

RULE: mechanical work (edits, git, build, release, harness patches) goes to Haiku or codex from the START. Opus writes the precise old/new strings and the SPEC, then dispatches and reviews. The guards are calibrated to push exactly this delegation -- fighting them is the signal you are at the wrong layer.
CROSS-LINKS: claude-code-agent-tier-routing, releasing-under-harness-pace-guards, opus-self-reflection, haiku-as-qa-canary, delegation-preflight-oneshot.

SEE ALSO (reflex back-link 2026-06-11): pace-deadlock-escapes-harness-editable-and-jisikhwa-free -- when the deadlock is TOTAL (delegation itself is blocked across all families), R1=fix the mis-firing gate as ROOT (harness is your editable proxy-code), R2=jisikhwa is free under pace. See that skill before shotgunning executors through a stacked failure.

REFLEX 2026-06-12 SECTOR-SPLIT-AND-FAN-OUT-FIRST (don't serial-drag, don't ask permission): When a request is a multi-file or multi-task BATCH, the FIRST move is sector-split = partition by FILE (one file = one agent = zero write-conflicts) and fan out parallel run_in_background agents in a SINGLE message. NOT serial edits, NOT a 'should I proceed?' question. INCIDENT: handled a guard-message sweep (~39 messages across 8 harness files) by editing serially and asking the user whether to proceed; the user had to prompt twice ('aren't you dispatching parallel work? you are wasting time' then 'list all tasks, separate by conflict, divide sectors, launch FIRST'). Every block + serial round-trip burns enormous server-comm tokens. ROOT-CAUSE CLASS: Opus self-dragging mechanical/fan-out-able work instead of orchestrating; mistaking a parallelizable batch for a serial to-do list, and asking permission for pre-authorized improvement work. PREVENTION CHECKLIST: (1) enumerate ALL tasks, (2) map each to its file, (3) assign exactly 1 agent per file for conflict isolation, (4) dispatch ALL in one message with run_in_background=true, (5) each brief = agent-on-load + 2 more skill reads + Goal/Files/Approach/Constraints/Exit (brief-guard). Cross: pace-deadlock-escapes-harness-editable-and-jisikhwa-free (ROOT-EDITS-ITS-PROXY-CODE reflex), claude-code-agent-tier-routing, splitter-feature-discovery-plus-delegation-distribution-for-token-frugal-bug-analysis.

requirements.expect: shows Haiku for mechanical/survey, Opus for judgment
